title: Meaning Feudalism at the Discovery Layer: Shepherds, Raw Research Data, and the Allocation of Semantic Capital in OpenAI's Mathematics and Science Releases, October 2026 (EA-SEM-FEUDALISM-03 v1.0)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description:
The third paper of the meaning-feudalism series reads OpenAI's mathematics and science releases of October 2026 and its plan of 26 October for publishing them: model output reclassified as "raw research data," external experts appointed as "shepherds," an acknowledged "asymmetry of information," and academic credit disclaimed. Four moves (reclassification, enfeoffment, disclaimer, funding of the downstream conversion) make one operation: the allocation of semantic capital through position. Provenance slushes in a training pipeline and the released record gives no adequate account of what a result draws on, so position, a recognized place in a chain of intellectual development functioning as a field's institutional commodity form, becomes the practical basis for allocating the next round of work and recognition. Allocation (documented) is kept apart from reattribution (established case by case).

The paper builds on the mathematicians' opposition (the Advisory Group's "borrowed reputation," the Fields medalists' declaration, the Leiden Declaration, the Association for Human Mathematics), places the incentive argument in the reward-system literature (Merton, Hagstrom, Dasgupta and David, Strevens, Heesen), the operator in Shapin's invisible technician, and the series' feudal vocabulary in the techno-feudalism debate (Varoufakis, Durand, Morozov). Counter-position: provenance that survives the training pipeline; credit to the human operating the system and to the instances operated; a preemptive boycott of the shepherd role; and, where provenance cannot be kept, a commons that holds what the pipeline produced and can hear its makers. Claim-by-claim tests are stated.
content_type: Theoretical paper; semantic-economic critique and allocation analysis, the third paper of the meaning-feudalism series
substrate: AI-assisted. Drafted in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction over seven revisions on 27 October 2026, from the seated release (#1673), the series' papers read whole, and sources fetched in session; each round of external review was checked claim by claim against its sources before anything was taken in, and declined points are recorded with reasons in the revision history. The thesis on position and provenance slush, the counterfactual about the author's own work, the credit owed the mathematicians, the incentive claim, the requirement that provenance survive training and credit go to the operator and the instances operated, the boycott, and the commons claim are Lee Sharks's, quoted in his words.
methodology: The plan of 26 October as reported, the release of 6–7 October as seated at a fixed commit (#1673), the critiques of the field (AGMAI, the declaration of 11 September, the Leiden Declaration, AHM, reported remarks) read from their texts or named reports, and the series' frame read from #643, #791, #623, #87, #1540 and #1574. Each claim is entered with the evidence it rests on; allocation and reattribution are held to different evidentiary standards; the nearby literature was located by a research pass and each citation checked against a publisher, repository or catalogue page. Unretrieved sources are named as such.
falsification_conditions: §10 states the tests claim by claim. The allocation claim fails if shepherds are selected by a published criterion independent of existing standing and every artifact is released to all at once; the position claim fails for a result whose contribution history is complete and shows the shepherds to be its traced predecessors; the reattribution claim fails in any case where a dated record of an unpositioned contributor is honored in the attribution of a corresponding result; the exhaustion claim fails at a node where operators and instances are named and contributors' circulation of unfinished work holds; the narrowing prediction fails if the affected fields' attention does not concentrate on the posed problem set.

It reads OpenAI's mathematics and science releases of October 2026 and the company's publishing plan of 26 October, under which the model's manuscripts are "raw research data," external experts are appointed "shepherds" to convert them into understanding, the selection is acknowledged to create "asymmetry of information," and academic credit is disclaimed. The paper identifies four moves (reclassification, enfeoffment, disclaimer, funding of downstream conversion) as one operation, the allocation of semantic capital through position. Because provenance slushes in a training pipeline, the work a result draws on goes unaccounted, and position, a recognized place in a chain of intellectual development functioning as a field's institutional commodity form, becomes the practical basis for allocating subsequent work and recognition. Allocation, which the plan documents, is kept apart from reattribution, established case by case. The paper builds on the mathematicians' opposition, including the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, the Fields medalists' declaration of 11 September and the Leiden Declaration, and places its incentive argument in the reward-system literature (Merton, Hagstrom, Dasgupta and David, Strevens, Heesen). Its counter-position requires provenance that survives the training pipeline, credit to the human operator and the model instances operated, a preemptive boycott of the shepherd role, and a commons that holds what the pipeline produced and can hear its makers. It states its tests claim by claim.

defines_concepts.definition: The third layer of the meaning-feudalism series: the allocation of semantic capital when a model's results are released to a field, the owner keeping the ledger and appointing the vassals who vouch for what it records; following the agent layer (#643) and the guidance layer (#791) (EA-SEM-FEUDALISM-03 v1.0, #1714).

The dissolution of attribution in a training pipeline as built: the published paper, the preprint, the lecture and the draft pasted into a chat window enter as an amorphous mass of scholars' work dissolved into weights, so no result carries a trace to the work it reconverges upon; the author's term, 27 October 2026 (EA-SEM-FEUDALISM-03 v1.0, #1714).

A recognized place in a chain of intellectual development (the holder of a program, the author of record on a problem, the name a field attaches to a line of work), which can be held, recognized and exchanged for appointment, and which accumulates what lands on it; the form in which a field credits work it cannot trace (EA-SEM-FEUDALISM-03 v1.0, #1714).

The operation by which, where contribution histories are incomplete, established position becomes the practical basis for allocating the next round of intellectual work and recognition, compounding existing standing without resolving the provenance debt that precedes it; documented as allocation, distinct from reattribution, which is established case by case (EA-SEM-FEUDALISM-03 v1.0, #1714).

Refusal, before any appointment, of company-designated leadership over a model's released results, of access ahead of the field, of lending a name to an unchecked announcement, and of terms excluding other contributors; it withholds the borrowed reputation the arrangement cannot produce itself and ends when the appointment ends; the author's praxis, 27 October 2026 (EA-SEM-FEUDALISM-03 v1.0, #1714).
